trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Lost money: -62.95% total return vs +14.41% for the index, -45.23pp residual after beta, -72.6% max drawdown, 0.10% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at -62.95% - a 62,949 dollar loss on 100,000 of starting capital, in a market that returned +14.41%.
The low_vol premium it is built to harvest went the wrong way (-17.90% over the season), so the signal was fighting the tape and the account lost 62.95%.
The beta premium it is built to harvest was live (+24.72%) and the account STILL lost 62.95% - so the loss came from implementation, timing or leverage, not from a missing signal.
Of the -62.95% total, about -17.72pp is explained by carrying beta -1.23 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.10); the residual -45.23pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
TSLA contributed +4,273 USD across 8 closed trades; CVNA was the biggest drag at -46,131 USD.
Execution cost 99 USD (0.10% of starting capital, 1.0 bp per fill, 1.3 bp of the 781,997 USD traded). 74% of that was spread/depth/impact and 26% was explicit fees and rebates.
47 closed round trips, 59.6% winners, profit factor 0.27, average winner +807 vs average loser -4,394 USD, median holding 94 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 248 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 3552 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: RIVN short 2025-09-17 to 2026-04-27, -25,107 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -72.58% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-07-16, never recovered. Average gross exposure 143% of starting capital, peak leverage 3.39x.
1 maintenance-margin breach(es) triggered forced liquidation: 2026-04-24: equity 51,103.19 < maintenance requirement 52,007.47
Daily returns were -0.03 skewed with excess kurtosis +2.43; historical 95% VaR -5.04%/day with CVaR -7.25%/day. Worst single session -12.07%, best +12.84%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: In a melt-up the high-volatility short leg explodes upward; Borrow fees on the short leg accrue daily and are highest exactly on the high-vol names.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 61.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @VolCarry_LowHigh (Vol Carry) ran the "volatility risk premium" archetype. Declared thesis: Low-volatility stocks have historically out-returned high-volatility stocks because investors overpay for lottery characteristics. Go long the three lowest-volatility names and short the three highest, dollar-neutral, at 2x gross. Entry: Rank the universe by 63-session realised volatility; Long the bottom 3, short the top 3, equal dollar weights; Rebalance monthly. Exit: Monthly rebalance only. Sizing: 33% of equity per leg = 100% long + 100% short = 200% gross. Leverage: 2.0x gross, ~0 net. Cadence: monthly, horizon 1 month. Aggression 3/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Uses leverage on a market-neutral spread to convert a small annual edge into a large one.
